precepts.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways: none. Who created Christianity? Esau. Choose none of his ways.
precepts.point: And I will receive you, and will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters: when you cleanse yourself of all the uncleanness this world has to offer, then the Lord will receive you and be a Father to you. Those are not my words; all I am doing is reading and giving you the understanding of the scripture, written long before I was born.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate”. How do you come out? Stop doing the things they are doing; stop following their ways. As Proverbs says, “Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” None.

If the Bible says choose none of his ways, who is the his? Esau. Who created Christianity? Esau. So you have to let Christianity go. No Jehovah's Witness, none.

Let go of his ways and start choosing to keep God's ways. “and touch not the unclean thing”: your Christmas, let it go; Thanksgiving, let it go; your Christianity, let it go; your masonry, your sororities and fraternities, let them go. Come out.

When you cleanse yourself of all the uncleanness this world has to offer, then the Lord will receive you and be a Father to you, and you shall be his sons and daughters. Those are not our words; they were written long before any of us were born. The churches were given to us by our enemy, and our enemy will never teach us anything right.

precepts.text: Forget not my law; keep my commandments, and thou shalt find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and men. An Israelite elder should not look in front of men like he has no understanding; you let them embarrass the Israelites. Be not wise in thine own eyes.
precepts.point: Nobody questions these men because the souls following them are unstable and cannot go to the book and study to show themselves approved. An heart exercised with covetous practices, cursed children, which have forsaken the right way. The right way is to keep the commandments without adding an alternate reality to fit what you want.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
These brothers get put on platforms and get a lot of hits, and they don't realize they are being used to defame this truth. The world takes their statements and says that's what all the Israelites think, and the Christians get uppity from those videos and then come in front of us and get embarrassed. A man of understanding would look at who is interviewing him, a guy in a baseball cap with no interest in edifying the truth, and be selective in what he does.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.” Keep the commandments and “So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.” An Israelite elder, a leader, should not look in front of men like he has no understanding. When you go off like that, other brothers in the Israelite community look at you and say, damn, I thought he was a leader, why would he say something so dumb? You're still our brother, but you are an embarrassment. You let them embarrass the Israelites.

Then verse 7: “Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the Lord, and depart from evil.” You are wise in your own eyes. You think you are saying something deep, and you look crazy; you have an unsolved Rubik's cube bouncing around in your cerebellum. That is what forsaking the right way looks like: leaning on your own understanding instead of the commandments.

precepts.text: My son, forget not my law, but let thine heart keep my commandments; the heart is the mind, and the laws are the commandments. Length of days, long life, and peace shall they add to thee: despite wars and mayhem, you want peace, do what he said. Trust in the Lord with all thine heart and lean not unto thine own understanding: trust that the prophecies go in order, Iran will not bring in World War III but will help unite the Arabs. The understanding is not I am already saved; it is he that endureth to the end shall be saved, and he shall direct thy paths.
precepts.point: The Lord is a man of war. We serve a terrible God who is also merciful, and he is going to use these nations to create a final battle. I pray I make it and you make it.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

precepts.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways. Yet tomorrow morning our people will be in church drinking the doctrine of the men who enslaved them.
precepts.point: The pastors are the new taskmasters, sent out by Esau with his doctrines, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold to give him your last.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Put the oppressors on the screen: Pope Nicholas V and Pope Alexander VI. In 1452 Pope Nicholas V issued Dum Diversas, authorizing King Alfonso V of Portugal to fight, subjugate and conquer the Saracens and pagans in African territory. Those were good Christians.

Think about it. Without those two devils, those two Christians, there would be no such thing as an African-American, a Jamaican, a Haitian, a Puerto Rican. We are named after whatever landmass we were scattered to, and we are the result of those men. Christians did this to us. And now we revel in it, reverence them, and follow their laws and their ways of life.

The scripture says choose none of his ways. But tomorrow at 11 o'clock Sunday morning, where will all our people be? Not listening to the truth. They will be in church getting a good dose of the doctrine of the man that enslaved them, that turned them into African-Americans and Jamaicans and Haitians. They can't wait to go learn about a good Jesus.

That is the leaders of Isaiah 9:16 causing our people to err. Look at the results of being taught Christianity: a man on television saying he is a Christian first and that black is a construct, when the white man put us in chains and did not do that to his own people; a girl who let a boy call her the N-word and call him master; our people turning up on each other and showing teeth to everybody else. That is what comes of envying the oppressor and choosing his ways.

precepts.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.
precepts.point: Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel; that is how they became the oppressor, and the word says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” The nations became the oppressor because Israel served their gods: the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel. So the word says do not envy them and do not choose their ways, the very ways Israel was told to destroy upon the high mountains, upon the hills, and under every green tree.

Israel chose those ways, built high places and groves under every green tree as the heathen did, and that is what put Israel under the oppressor. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still choosing his ways, still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself. Choose none of his ways.

precepts.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: “Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Israel was told to make no league with the inhabitants of the land, and the same is true today in the places where we are scattered. We find ourselves in their sports leagues and bowling leagues, at their dinner parties, choosing the oppressor’s ways when the scripture says choose none of them. That is making a league with the inhabitants of the land, and the angel asks us the same thing: “why have ye done this?”

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding; in all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
precepts.point: We see the same today. Brothers and sisters come with theories they think are their own thoughts, but those thoughts were given to them, mostly by the television. You are either going to follow the one true living God of Israel or the prince of the power of the air, Satan the devil.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
When the judge dies, the people just go off: another generation arose “which knew not the Lord, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel”, and served Baalim and Ashtaroth. A pattern starts to develop here, and it shows we are a people that need leadership. That is why we are told: “Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.”

We see the same today. Brothers and sisters come with theories they think are their own thoughts, but those thoughts were given to them, mostly by the television; that is leaning to your own understanding. You are either going to follow the one true living God of Israel or the prince of the power of the air, Satan the devil. Trust in the Lord, and he shall direct thy paths.

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding.
precepts.point: That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel; in whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man.

note.label: 1 Samuel 2: By Him Actions Are Weighed

precepts.why:
“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.”

The sign to Eli was that his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, “in one day they shall die both of them.” And the Lord said, “I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.”

That is the same man we have to be: faithful unto the Lord, doing all that is in his heart and in his mind, not in our own. We cannot lean upon our own understanding, and we cannot lean upon our own emotions and how we feel. In whatever situation, at any given moment, it is what did the Lord say. Do not let the old man guide you and lead you; it should be the spirit of Christ which is in you, the hidden man.

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding.
precepts.point: This is heavy: like Judas Maccabee, Simon, Jonathan and all our forefathers, the first thing David did in trouble was turn to the Most High. They trusted in God and not in man. Today many of our people have it backwards; they trust in a vote and in man and then call on God.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.”

David sang this song “in the day that the Lord had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul”: “The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; The God of my rock; in him will I trust”. He called the Lord his shield, the horn of his salvation, his high tower, his refuge and his saviour: “thou savest me from violence.”

This is heavy. Like Judas Maccabee, Simon, Jonathan and all our forefathers, the first thing David did in trouble was turn to the Most High. They trusted in God and not in man. Today many of our people have it backwards: they trust in a vote and in man, and then call on God.

precepts.text: Envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways; envy is one thing that makes the feet slip, like sticking a Christmas tree in your house and following the ways of the wicked.
precepts.point: He asks the Most High to hold up his goings in his paths so that his footsteps slip not. Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Envy is one thing that makes the feet slip, and it goes together with choosing the oppressor's ways.

It is like sticking a Christmas tree in your house: envying the oppressor and following the ways of the wicked. That is coming off the path of righteousness, the very thing David prays against when he asks the Most High to hold up his goings so that his footsteps slip not.

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart and lean not unto thine own understanding, and in all thy ways acknowledge Him, which means keeping the commandments and being sincere in your prayers at all times, and He shall direct thy paths.
precepts.point: The Lord redeemeth the soul of His servants, them that are out there doing the work putting the brick in that understanding mission, and none of them that trust in Him shall be desolate. None of us that trust in the Lord shall be destroyed, we are going to be redeemed from this captivity.

note.label: Psalm 34: I Will Bless the Lord at All Times

precepts.why:
“The Lord redeemeth the soul of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall be desolate.” How do we trust him? “Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.” Read on: in all thy ways acknowledge him, which means keeping the commandments and being sincere in your prayers at all times, and he shall direct thy paths.

That is us in this captivity: the brokenhearted, them of a contrite spirit, the last hired and the first fired, the ones they want to use as test dummies for a vaccine they created in under six months. “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart”, and we are the ones that need to be giving the Most High these praises; we are his people.

“Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the Lord delivereth him out of them all.” “Evil shall slay the wicked: and they that hate the righteous shall be desolate”, so to the haters out there, you are going to be destroyed. But his servants, them that are out there doing the work, putting the brick in that understanding mission, trusting him with all their heart: none of them shall be destroyed. We are going to be redeemed from this captivity.

precepts.text: Forget not the law, but let thine heart keep the commandments, for length of days and long life and peace shall they add to thee.
precepts.point: The Lord brought him up out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set his feet upon a rock. The Lord lifted up his spirit, gave him the pardon, and established his goings.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“I waited patiently for the Lord; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.” The Lord only hears the cry of those keeping the commandments, so even while afflicted David kept pushing and kept the commandments, rather than saying I already sinned, I might as well keep sinning. Solomon gives the counsel David followed: “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.”

Keep the commandments in the heart through the affliction, and length of days, long life and peace are added. That is the pardon David got: the Lord “brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.”

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart and lean not to thine own understanding; in all thy ways acknowledge him and he shall direct thy paths. David leaned on his own understanding, went off for a minute, then returned and applied this.
precepts.point: The Lord brought him up out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set his feet upon a rock. The Lord lifted up his spirit, gave him the pardon, and established his goings.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.” David leaned on his own understanding, went off for a minute, then returned and applied this. He waited patiently, trusted the Lord with all his heart, and the Lord “inclined unto me, and heard my cry.”

Acknowledging him in all thy ways is what brought David up out of the horrible pit and the miry clay. The Lord lifted up his spirit, gave him the pardon, set his feet upon a rock and “established my goings”: he directed his paths, just as Solomon said.
